# DiscoPoP B19 and B18 — a wrong `lastprivate` in three places and the Do-All that nests with counters declared at the top of the function had lost: the repairs and their regression check

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

After the explorer's repairs of 8 Oct (a last value assigned in only some passes blocks Do-All; an array is shared; only a loop's own units decide its clauses; a write-after-read is attached to units by its own roles): does DiscoPoP alone give every one of the 44 tsvc_c3 packages its measured class, with a difference only where the repairs aim (s331, s481), and what does it now say on the 31 packages outside TSVC?

## Result in one paragraph

Passed on TSVC: on the 44 tsvc_c3 packages every class and every draw is as before the repairs; DiscoPoP offers other directives on the two loops the repairs aim at and nowhere else (s331: nothing offered any more; s481: the kept directive without lastprivate(nl)). Outside TSVC, correlation, covariance and fdtd-2d have their outer loop's directive back in 3 of 3 draws (medians 5.7×, 5.7×, 4.2×) — nine loops given back by the B18 repair, none lost. Two things the draws showed that are not the repairs': on PolyBench the explorer, on one profile, blocks every loop that carries an observed dependence or none of them, never a part, and blocks none in 57 of 81 profiles (B21, measured, not traced) — gramschmidt's loop comes back only in such draws (2 of 3); and a rule of DiscoPoP's own calls a loop parallel whose pass reads an array element a later pass overwrites (B22, new: adi's last nest, refused by the gate in 3 of 3 draws; on TSVC hidden by B16). One regression of the array repair showed in those draws, on burkardt/md (the force loop's work array rij shared where each thread needs its own; refused by the gate) and was corrected the same day: an array that a function the loop calls writes keeps its private clause. RE-CHECK on the corrected explorer, six more draws (t0_11_c3_b19r_a–c, t0_11_b19r_apps_a–c): the 44 TSVC packages as on the first repair in every class, outcome, directive, clause and verdict; md's loop with its private work array again in 3 of 3 draws; what else differs outside TSVC is draw-to-draw (B21 and the order of DiscoPoP's patterns), not the correction. After nine draws: the explorer blocks all such loops in 65 PolyBench profiles, none in 133, some in 0; five kernels never seen blocking. A blocked loop's record names one of the loop's dependences and which one differs between runs — the variable on 40 of 44 TSVC packages, on s244 also the type. Found on the way, in our own gate: its dependence stage compares the working file's line numbers with the profile's and refused one correct directive on mvt (once in the whole archive; repair proposed before E7). No model in any of it.

| 2026-10-08 | DiscoPoP | **B19 repaired and B18 traced and repaired, both in the explorer and verified on the Mac; two further defects found on the way (B20, B21: candidates, not repaired). The server's draws are registered with this row and launched after it; no model is involved.** **B19 — three mechanisms, three repairs** (`pattern_detectors/new_do_all_detector.py`; `discopop_agent/docs/DISCOPOP_BUG_REPORTS.md` has the detail). (1) *A last value assigned in only some passes* (`s331`): the detector's modelled iterations cannot tell a conditional assignment from one every pass makes; the control flow can — with the assigning units taken out, a pass must not get from its first unit back to it. Such a loop is no longer reported Do-All (DiscoPoP has no clause for "the last assignment"); the record it leaves is the write-after-write between passes on the assignment's line, marked observed where the profile holds the assignment overwriting itself. Only a loop that would otherwise be reported is concerned. (2) *Arrays:* the test that keeps a pointer's target `shared` looked for `*` or `&` in the type; `real_t[32000]` has neither. An array is now `shared` on the loop that fills it and on the one that reads it. (3) *`s481`:* with `exit(0)` in the inner loop's body the task graph puts units of the loop around it into the inner loop's iterations; a loop's clauses are now decided by its own units and what they call. The modelling defect itself is B20. **B18 — traced:** the explorer of the commit before B10's fix (`9a86f4855`) and the explorer of that fix (`8c7e6066f`) on ONE kept profile of `polybench/correlation`: before, the loops at lines 98, 106, 109 are Do-All with their inner counters private; after, blocked on a static RAW on the counter. So the change that took the Do-All away is B10's fix — ours — and the reason is older code it met: `PEGraphX.from_parsed_input` attaches a write-after-read to the units of its lines by a read-after-write's roles, so on a one-line `for (j = 0; j < m; j++)` the unit that only initialises `j` is credited with the condition's and the increment's reads; B10's rule (a read and a write of one variable on one line in one unit: read first) then makes the counter read-first, and it is no longer privatizable. **Repaired** in `classes/PEGraph/PEGraphX.py`: a write-after-read is attached by its own roles; where a line has no unit in the right role the old lookup stays.
